title: TrackScout questions document
description: Served at GET /data/owner_questions.json and shipped as examples/demo_questions.json. The app downloads it whole on every sync; questions are matched by id across regenerations, so keep ids stable. `tools/validate_questions.py` validates a file against this schema before you publish it.

generated.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the latest regeneration. Informational: it tells agents and the app when the file was last built, but nothing keys on it.

questions.description: The questions. `minItems: 1` so an empty document is a validation error, not a silent no-questions app.

groups.description: Optional display order of the free-form `group` labels, as the project intends them shown (most important first). When absent, the app orders places alphabetically.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the document. Keep it stable across regenerations: re-answers and photos attach by this id, and changing it orphans them. No whitespace. Internal project ids (e.g. geodata keys, dossier paths) may sit alongside it in the file but are never shown in the app.

page.description: Pager page number within the place.

order.description: Position within the page. The app shows open questions first, in (page, order) sequence.

group.description: Free-form label, e.g. a tier or area name. The All tab sections places by group, in the document's `groups` order (falling back to alphabetical).

building.description: The place's display name. Several questions normally share one building (and one point); the app groups them into a single place.

lat.description: WGS-84 latitude of a point on the pavement facing the subject, not the building centroid: the owner walks there to answer.

context.description: One short line of background the owner needs to answer, e.g. what a reference photo shows and what the current guess is. Shown above the question in the app.

question.description: One question per decision, phrased for a non-expert standing on the pavement. Yes/no where possible.

type.description: `yesno` shows Yes/No; `choice` shows one button per entry of `options` (2-5, checked by the validator); `text` is a free-text field. Every type also offers Don't know, sent as the answer text `Don't know`.

options.description: Answer options for `choice`; must be empty for `yesno` and `text` (the validator enforces this). 2-5 for choice.

images.description: 0-3 reference images shown with the question (e.g. look-around stills, a prior photo, a plan).

photo_wanted.description: Optional (photo capture): which photos the project wants for this question. `day` = normal light, `night` = after dark (lit signage, lit windows), `both`. Absent = no photo is requested; questions files without the field keep working.

question.description: Additional properties are allowed and ignored by the app: projects may carry internal ids (geodata keys, dossier paths) in their questions file. They never reach the UI, so never store private data in them.

src.description: Either a path relative to the questions file - the reference server serves it at GET /qimg/<url-encoded path> - or a full https:// URL, which the app loads directly. Relative paths must stay inside the questions file's directory (the server rejects escaping paths).

caption.description: Optional one-line caption shown under the image.
